deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §22 of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page dealt with the zeros of θ(u−e) and the additive constants k_μ. This page sets up the residue/contour argument that fixes the position of the p zeros η_1..η_p of θ(u_1−e_1,…,u_p−e_p) on the Riemann surface T. The page ends just as the boundary integral is introduced.

Setting (Riemann's normalisation). u_μ are normalised integrals of the first kind. The cuts a_ν, b_ν dissect T into the simply connected surface T'. Across a_ν, u_μ has period πi·δ_{μν}; across b_ν it has period a_{μν}. The theta function is θ(v) = Σ_m exp(Σ a_{μμ'} m_μ m_μ' + 2Σ v_μ m_μ). Its quasi-periodicity is θ(v + πi e_ν) = θ(v) and θ(v + a_{·ν}) = exp(−2v_ν − a_{νν}) θ(v).

(1) Monodromy of log θ(u−e) in T'.
- θ(u−e) has p simple zeros η. So a positive circuit of (s,z) around one zero η increases log θ by 2πi (argument principle for a simple zero).
- A positive circuit around a cut pair (a_ν, b_ν), i.e. around the boundary piece of T' formed by the four banks, increases log θ by −2πi.
- My filling: the jump −2(u_ν−e_ν) from crossing b_ν, integrated as u_ν runs over a_ν, contributes −2·πi. The total over all p pairs is −2πi·p. This balances the +2πi·p from the p zeros, as it must for a single-valued function on T'.

(2) Making log θ single-valued.
- From each zero η draw a cut l through the interior to the common start/end point of one pair a_ν, b_ν. This gives the surface T*.
- Take log θ(u−e) continuous in T*.
- Its jumps (value on the + side minus value on the − side) are:
  - across l: −2πi;
  - across a_ν: g_ν·2πi;
  - across b_ν: −2(u_ν−e_ν) − a_{νν} + h_ν·2πi.
  - Here g_ν and h_ν are integers.
- The b_ν jump is the logarithm of the theta factor exp(−2v_ν − a_{νν}), with v = u−e, plus an undetermined branch 2πi·h_ν. The a_ν jump is only a branch multiple, because θ is πi-periodic in each v_ν.

(3) Programme stated at the end.
- The positions η and the integers g, h depend on the e's.
- This dependence is to be found by evaluating ∫ log θ du_μ positively around the boundary of T*. The integral vanishes by Cauchy, since log θ and u_μ are holomorphic and single-valued in T*.
- In the published version, evaluating the boundary contributions gives Σ_ν u_μ(η_ν) ≡ e_μ − k_μ modulo periods, with k_μ given explicitly. That is the 'easier way' to the constants promised on the previous page.
- The computation itself is not on this page.
errors: Expression ambiguity: the b_ν jump −2(u_ν−e_ν) − a_{νν} leaves implicit on which bank u_ν is taken. This only matters for the sign of the a_{νν} term, and Riemann's choice matches his published text.
Crossed-out passages show hesitation over how to route the cuts l (to a common point of all pairs vs. to the common point of each pair). The final choice is consistent.

results.what: Argument-principle monodromy of log θ(u−e) on the dissected Riemann surface: +2πi around each zero, −2πi around each cut pair
results.modern_name: Argument principle on a canonically dissected surface; count of zeros of the theta divisor pullback (= g)

results.what: Jumps of log θ(u−e) across a_ν, b_ν from theta quasi-periodicity: g_ν·2πi and −2(u_ν−e_ν) − a_{νν} + 2πi·h_ν
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity (automorphy factor) of the Riemann theta function

results.what: Plan to determine the zeros η via the contour integral ∮ log θ du_μ = 0 around T*, leading to Σ u(η_ν) ≡ e − k
results.modern_name: Riemann's vanishing theorem (first part) / Riemann constant vector

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material printed almost verbatim in §22 of Riemann's 1857 Crelle paper on Abelian functions. It is well known as his.
